era: Mid-2000s and seventh-generation psychological horror shooters
summary: Monolith Productions' psychological horror FPS series, including TimeGate's standalone expansions and the later shutdown F.E.A.R. Online.

entries.title: F.E.A.R.
entries.definitive_edition: F.E.A.R. Platinum on Windows for main play; console ports for bonus missions

emulation.emulator: Native Windows, Xenia, or RPCS3 where legal and stable
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main run; use console hardware/emulation only for the two bonus missions.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC main game, with console-exclusive bonus content as supplements

primary.why: F.E.A.R. originated on Windows, then received Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 ports with their own bonus missions and weapons. Windows remains the highest-fidelity main route, especially through modern PC preservation releases, while the console ports are secondary only for their exclusive bonus missions.
primary.how_to_play: Play F.E.A.R. Platinum on Windows for the main run; then check the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 bonus missions only if you want the console-exclusive material.

secondary.exclusive_content: Exclusive bonus level about Holiday extracting Bishop plus dual automatic handguns
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 bonus level after the Windows main run.
secondary.why: The Xbox 360 port includes a bonus level and weapon content not in the original PC release.

secondary.exclusive_content: Exclusive bonus mission about Delta Force's route through ATC headquarters plus street sweeper shotgun
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PS3 bonus mission after the Windows main run.
secondary.why: The PS3 port includes a different bonus mission and weapon from the Xbox 360/PC versions.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC release; later Platinum/modern PC preservation bundles include the two standalone expansions.
Console port equivalent to PC maximum settings with 720p, HDR, advanced particles, HD textures, plus an exclusive bonus level and weapon.
all_releases.reason: secondary: exclusive bonus level/weapon content; not the main route over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Console port with its own exclusive bonus mission and street sweeper shotgun, but some Xbox 360 enhancements removed.
all_releases.reason: secondary: exclusive bonus mission/weapon content; not the main route over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the fidelity and preservation route, but Xbox 360 and PS3 each have different exclusive bonus missions/weapons; play those as secondary extras only.

entries.remaster_caveats: Modern PC availability is preservation-focused rather than a remaster; console bonus missions remain outside the PC main route.

entries.title: F.E.A.R. Extraction Point
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC expansion for main play; F.E.A.R. Files for collection bonus maps

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or Xbox backward compatibility where owned
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the expansion campaign; use Xbox only for F.E.A.R. Files bonus maps.

primary.why: Extraction Point released first on Windows and later on Xbox 360 only inside F.E.A.R. Files. Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the expansion, while the Xbox 360 F.E.A.R. Files package contains extra instant-action and multiplayer maps at the collection level.
primary.how_to_play: Play Extraction Point on Windows through F.E.A.R. Platinum or a standalone legal copy; check F.E.A.R. Files only for its extra map content if desired.

secondary.exclusive_content: F.E.A.R. Files collection bonus instant-action and multiplayer maps
secondary.what_to_play: Check the F.E.A.R. Files bonus maps after the PC expansion if preserving every collection-level mode/map matters.
secondary.why: The Xbox 360 package includes extra instant-action and multiplayer maps beyond the two expansion campaigns.

all_releases.fidelity: Standalone PC expansion, later included in Gold/Platinum PC collections and GOG/Steam preservation releases.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most accessible expansion route.

all_releases.fidelity: Released only inside F.E.A.R. Files, with collection-level bonus instant-action and multiplayer maps.
all_releases.reason: secondary: extra map content in the F.E.A.R. Files package, but PC remains the main expansion route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the best expansion route, but F.E.A.R. Files adds collection-level maps worth noting for completeness.

entries.remaster_caveats: The expansion is no longer canon to the Monolith-developed sequel line, but it remains a released standalone expansion.

entries.title: F.E.A.R. Perseus Mandate
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC expansion for main play; F.E.A.R. Files for collection bonus maps

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or Xbox backward compatibility where owned
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the expansion campaign; use Xbox only for F.E.A.R. Files bonus maps.

primary.how_to_play: Play Perseus Mandate on Windows through F.E.A.R. Platinum or a standalone legal copy; check F.E.A.R. Files only if you want the extra map content.

secondary.exclusive_content: F.E.A.R. Files collection bonus instant-action and multiplayer maps
secondary.what_to_play: Check the F.E.A.R. Files bonus maps after the PC expansion if preserving every collection-level mode/map matters.
secondary.why: The Xbox 360 package includes extra instant-action and multiplayer maps beyond the two expansion campaigns.

all_releases.fidelity: Standalone PC expansion, later included in Platinum Collection and GOG/Steam preservation releases.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most accessible expansion route.

all_releases.fidelity: Released inside F.E.A.R. Files with collection-level bonus instant-action and multiplayer maps.
all_releases.reason: secondary: extra map content in F.E.A.R. Files, but PC remains the main expansion route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the best expansion route, but F.E.A.R. Files adds collection-level maps worth noting for completeness.

entries.remaster_caveats: The expansion is no longer canon to the Monolith-developed sequel line, but it remains a released standalone expansion.

entries.title: F.E.A.R. 2: Project Origin
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC version with Reborn DLC where owned

emulation.notes: Use Windows rather than emulating PS3/Xbox 360.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC version with Reborn DLC

primary.version: PC version with Reborn DLC where owned
primary.why: F.E.A.R. 2 released simultaneously on PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360, with the Reborn single-player DLC released later in 2009. Windows is the highest-fidelity route and should include Reborn for content completeness.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with F.E.A.R. 2: Reborn installed if owned; use console versions as equivalent original-platform routes.

all_releases.fidelity: Native PC release; Reborn DLC adds a four-mission single-player campaign.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity route and supports the documented DLC path.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release with Reborn DLC available as platform DLC.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release with Reborn DLC available as platform DLC and later backward compatibility.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows with Reborn installed is the fidelity and content-complete route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster is documented in the cited public source; GOG availability helps preserve the PC release.

entries.title: F.E.A.R. 3

emulation.notes: Use Windows/GOG for the main run; Xbox backward compatibility is a console convenience route.

primary.why: F.E.A.R. 3 released on PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360 in 2011, later becoming available on GOG and Xbox backward compatibility. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/GOG version natively; use console versions only for original-platform comparison or co-op convenience.

all_releases.fidelity: Native PC release with later GOG availability.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most flexible route.
skip: no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release with later Xbox backward compatibility.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content requires a secondary route; Windows is the fidelity/access pick.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster is documented in the cited public source.

entries.title: F.E.A.R. Online
entries.definitive_edition: No active definitive edition; Windows archival documentation only

emulation.emulator: No stable live-service emulation route documented
emulation.notes: Treat as an unavailable online entry unless a legal server/client preservation route is found.

primary.why: F.E.A.R. Online was a Windows free-to-play online entry released in 2014, but its servers were shut down in 2015 while still in open beta. Windows is the only sourced platform and this entry is archival rather than a normal play recommendation.
primary.how_to_play: No normal live-service route is documented after the 2015 shutdown; preserve through footage, documentation, and any legal retained client/server research.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced platform; shutdown free-to-play online game.
all_releases.reason: primary: archival documentation route only because the servers shut down in 2015.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one sourced platform release exists; the limiting factor is server shutdown.

entries.remaster_caveats: Servers shut down in 2015 while the game was still in open beta.
